originality.rationale: The 2023 model paper restricts its Poisson-convolution investigation to positive transmutation and gives no thinning-self-decomposability classification. The 2016 parent distribution paper defines the negative range and its maximum endpoint but likewise does not classify it. Known classical canonical-sequence theory is used rather than claimed. A related full-text geometric-maximum theorem establishes additive infinite divisibility for the boundary but not the requested stronger thinning property. The closest separately inspected geometric folding theorem is algebraically different. The explicit two-comparison reduction and reentrant negative-transmutation parameter examples are not implied by these prior statements; priority remains qualified.
residual_risks: Not all possibly relevant classical geometrically compounded count-law literature is indexed or fully searchable.
This is a same-model scientific review; no independent audit or global historical priority certification.

value.rationale: The complete naturally defined negative-transmutation parameter class contains all three structural regimes: Poisson-recoverable thinning self-decomposability, non-rescuable loss despite ordinary compound-Poisson divisibility, and reentrant phase transitions at fixed q and lambda. The exact two-index reduction is a meaningful finite cutoff for an otherwise infinite canonical sequence.
